idea.body: In a right triangle, pick one of the two acute angles and call it A. The side across from A is opposite. The side next to A that is not the hypotenuse is adjacent. The longest side, across from the right angle, is the hypotenuse. Sine of A is opposite over hypotenuse, cosine of A is adjacent over hypotenuse, and tangent of A is opposite over adjacent. A robot's arm brace is a right triangle with legs 3 centimeters and 4 centimeters and hypotenuse 5 centimeters. If A is opposite the 3 centimeter leg, sine of A is 3/5, cosine of A is 4/5, and tangent of A is 3/4. These ratios stay the same for any triangle with the same angle, no matter its size.

figure.alt: A right triangle with legs 3 and 4, the angle at the marked vertex highlighted.

workedExample.prompt: A rover's antenna brace is a right triangle with legs 6 centimeters and 8 centimeters and hypotenuse 10 centimeters. Angle A is opposite the 6 centimeter leg. Find cosine of A.
steps: Angle A is opposite the 6 centimeter leg, so the 6 centimeter leg is the opposite side.
The 8 centimeter leg is next to A and is not the hypotenuse, so it is the adjacent side.
Cosine compares the adjacent side to the hypotenuse: 8 over 10.
Reduce 8/10 to lowest terms: cosine of A = 4/5.

figure.alt: A right triangle with legs 6 and 8, the angle at the marked vertex highlighted.

ways.name: SOH CAH TOA
ways.when: Use this any time you know all three sides of a right triangle.
steps: SOH CAH TOA names sine, cosine and tangent as ratios of the sides.
A brace is a right triangle with legs 9 and 12 centimeters and hypotenuse 15 centimeters.
Angle A is opposite the 9 centimeter leg, so 9 is opposite and 12 is adjacent.
Sine of A is opposite over hypotenuse: 9/15, which reduces to 3/5.
Cosine of A is adjacent over hypotenuse: 12/15, which is 4/5. Tangent is 9/12, or 3/4.
ways.example: A right triangle has legs 9 and 12 centimeters and hypotenuse 15 centimeters. Angle A is opposite the 9 centimeter leg. Find sine, cosine and tangent of A.
ways.answer: sin A = 3/5, cos A = 4/5, tan A = 3/4
ways.trap: Mixing up which leg is opposite and which is adjacent once the reference angle changes.

figure.alt: A right triangle with legs 9 and 12 centimeters, angle A marked at one acute vertex.

frames.caption: A is opposite the 9 cm leg

ways.name: Label the sides first
ways.when: Use this when it is easy to mix up which leg is opposite and which is adjacent.
steps: A strut is a right triangle with legs 8 and 15 centimeters and hypotenuse 17 centimeters.
Mark the right angle first, then the hypotenuse: the longest side, across from it, 17 centimeters.
Pick angle B and mark the side across from it as opposite: the 8 centimeter leg.
Mark the remaining leg, next to B and not the hypotenuse, as adjacent: 15 centimeters.
Only now compute cosine of B: adjacent over hypotenuse, 15/17.
ways.example: A right triangle has legs 8 and 15 centimeters and hypotenuse 17 centimeters. Angle B is opposite the 8 centimeter leg. Find cosine of B.
ways.trap: Computing a ratio before marking opposite and adjacent, then mixing the two legs up.

figure.alt: A right triangle with its hypotenuse, opposite side and adjacent side tagged, angle B marked.

frames.caption: Right triangle, sides to be labeled.
Angle B; opposite is the 8 cm leg
Adjacent leg, not the hypotenuse: 15 cm

ways.name: Spot the scaled triple
ways.when: Use this when the three sides share a common factor with a known triple.
steps: A ramp brace is a right triangle with legs 30 and 40 centimeters and hypotenuse 50 centimeters.
30, 40 and 50 are each 10 times 3, 4 and 5: a 3-4-5 triangle scaled by 10.
Angle A is opposite the 30 centimeter leg, matching the 3 in the triple.
Read the ratio straight from the triple: sine of A is 3/5, no long division needed.
ways.example: A right triangle has legs 30 and 40 centimeters and hypotenuse 50 centimeters. Angle A is opposite the 30 centimeter leg. Find sine of A.
ways.trap: Computing 30/50 the long way instead of spotting the shared factor of 10 first.
